artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a nonconstant polynomial or rational function $f:\mathbb{C}\to\hat{\mathbb{C}}$ of degree $N\ge 1$, define
$$
I(r,f) \;=\; \frac{1}{r}\int_{0}^{r}\!\!\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} \frac{|f'(\rho e^{i\theta})|}{1+|f(\rho e^{i\theta})|^{2}}\, d\theta\, d\rho ,
$$
and set
$$
\varphi(N) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\, I(r,f) : r>0,\ f\text{ a polynomial or rational function with }\deg f = N\,\bigr\}.
$$
The integrand is the spherical area density of $f$ at the point $\rho e^{i\theta}$.

(a) Determine the precise asymptotic behavior of $\varphi(N)$ as $N\to\infty$. It is known that
$$
\varphi(N) = O\!\left(N^{1/2}\right) \quad\text{and}\quad \varphi(N) \neq O\!\bigl((\log N)^{1/2-\varepsilon}\bigr)
$$
for every $\varepsilon>0$. Find the sharp order of growth, and in particular compute (or estimate sharply) $\varphi(N)$ for the small cases $N=2,3,4,\ldots$.

(b) Decide whether the analogous unrestricted functional
$$
J(f) \;=\; \int_{0}^{\infty}\!\!\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} \frac{|f'(r e^{i\theta})|}{1+|f(re^{i\theta})|^{2}}\, d\theta\, dr
$$
is bounded, when $f$ ranges over polynomials or rational functions of degree $N$, by a quantity of the same order as $\varphi(N)$ — equivalently, prove that $\sup_{\deg f = N} J(f) < \infty$ and compare it with $\varphi(N)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Littlewood's conjecture on the average growth of the spherical derivative of polynomials of degree N was proved by J. Lewis and J.-M. Wu in 1988, establishing the conjectured upper bound. A. Eremenko later showed the bound is qualitatively sharp by lower estimates obtained via complex dynamics, and further work appears in "On the spherical derivative of a rational function" (arXiv:1207.5214). Thus the order of growth of φ(N) is essentially determined for polynomials, but a precise sharp constant/asymptotic and the small-N values requested, as well as full resolution for general rational functions and finiteness/comparability of the doubly-infinite functional J(f), are not completely settled.

status_evidence.title: On conjectures of Arakelyan and Littlewood (Lewis–Wu)
status_evidence.snippet: Lewis and Wu proved Littlewood's conjecture on the growth of the spherical derivative of polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: The polynomial case of Littlewood's spherical-derivative conjecture (giving the upper bound on φ(N)) was proved by Lewis and Wu.

status_evidence.title: Lower estimate in Littlewood's conjecture on the mean spherical derivative (Eremenko)
status_evidence.snippet: Eremenko applied complex iteration theory to show that the Lewis–Wu bound is sharp in a qualitative sense.
status_evidence.claim: Matching lower bounds, qualitatively sharp, are due to Eremenko via complex dynamics.

status_evidence.title: On the spherical derivative of a rational function
status_evidence.snippet: Estimates of the spherical derivative norm K(f) for rational f, individual functions and iterates.
status_evidence.claim: The rational case is studied with quantitative spherical-derivative estimates, but a fully sharp answer for all N and the unrestricted functional J(f) is not given.
